head: claude/r13-merge-slot-on-the-arming-route
title: pr-landing R13: the arming route takes the merge slot
body:
> ⚠️ **This file is the source of record for the PR body; GitHub's copy of PR #11344 is STALE.**
> The body was corrected here after the PR was opened, and a sub-session 403s on both
> `update_pull_request` and `add_issue_comment`, so the correction could not be pushed to
> GitHub. Where the two differ, **this file is right**. Corrected in code and docs by `66d0725`.

`WO-20260908-PR-LANDING-R6-AND-THE-MERGE-SLOT`.

## Summary

**The two guards are not in conflict, and the work order's framing does not survive reading the code.** R6 mandates a landing route on which the merge-slot guard is *structurally silent*, and the claim that would serialize it is unpostable. R13 puts the slot on that route. Neither existing rule is weakened.

⚠️ **The dispatch's description of R6 is wrong and worth correcting on the record.** It says R6 "guards that a manager holding a lease is actually supervising." R6 does nothing of the kind — `scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py:431` — it requires a branch declaring `landing: "self"` to have *armed* the route (`.github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt` added-or-modified vs base). Its stated purpose is that "a readiness declaration lands nothing on its own — that is precisely how 7 green PRs sat unmerged on 2026-09-03." No lease, no supervision.

## What was measured

Re-derived from both guards' code, not inherited.

| | |
|---|---|
| **R6** (`check_pr_landing.py:431`) | `landing: "self"` ⇒ the arming file must be added-or-modified vs base |
| **Merge-slot guard** (`.claude/settings.json`, `PreToolUse`) | matcher = `mcp__github__merge_pull_request\|mcp__github__enable_pr_auto_merge`; denies unless `/tmp/.claude-merge-claim-<sid>-<pr>` is fresh (<20 min) |
| **What arming actually does** | push to `claude/**` → `claude-pr-automerge.yml` enables auto-merge **as GitHub Actions under `GITHUB_TOKEN`** |

**The session calls no merge tool on the R6 route, so the hook cannot fire.** Reproduced by running the shipping hook command against synthetic stdin (population = the 4 tool names the arming route can use):

```
A. merge_pull_request, no slot claim                 -> deny   (control: the guard works on its own route)
B. matcher covers Bash                               -> False
B. matcher covers Write                              -> False
B. matcher covers mcp__github__push_files            -> False
B. matcher covers mcp__github__create_or_update_file -> False
```

**This is a different and larger hole than `BL-20260819-MERGE-SLOT-GUARD-DOES-NOT-FIRE`.** That one is "the guard does not load on the web." This one is "the guard is not on this road" — it holds in CLI and desktop too, where hooks *do* load.

### Why it looked mutually unsatisfiable

- Satisfy R6 → merge happens via Actions → no hook, no claim → **unclaimed merge, silently**.
- Claim the slot through the MCP route instead → no arming file in the diff → **R6 fails the PR** → auto-merge never fires → it never lands.

Doing *both* was always logically available — nothing in R6 forbids a claim. It is unavailable in *fact* because the authoritative claim is a `🔒 MERGE SLOT CLAIM` comment on **#6927, which is at GitHub's hard 2500-comment cap and 403s on write (MI-182)**.

**So MI-182 is not a parked side-nuisance; it is the proximate cause of this work order.** Corroborated by three independent prior sessions recording the same 403.

## The fix (R13)

A branch that ARMS must hold `merge_slot` in `docs/claude/session-board.json` — `held_by`, `branch`, `claimed_at` set to itself — **added-or-modified in its own diff**. That last part is load-bearing for the reason `claude-pr-automerge.yml`'s own REQUEST GATE gives: a branch that merely merged `main` while somebody else's claim sat on it has asked for nothing, and presence alone cannot tell the two apart.

Both invariants stay true:

- **R6 unchanged** — arming is still required.
- **The hook unchanged** — the MCP route is still guarded exactly as before.
- Being a **CI check rather than a hook**, R13 also holds on Claude Code on the web, where no project hook loads at all.

`session-board.json` already *is* the protocol's named durable record (`coordination-board.md` § Scope + limits). R13 enforces the mirror; it does not redefine which home is authoritative. When a successor board exists, the comment resumes as the live signal and R13 is unaffected.

## ⚠️ What R13 does NOT do

**R13 does not serialize anything.** `BL-20260810-MERGE-SLOT-MIRROR-UNWRITABLE-PRE-MERGE` (status `kept_open`) establishes why and still stands: `merge_slot` lives in a committed file, so a claim written on a branch **reaches no other session until that branch merges** — by which point the claim is over. Two branches can each arm, each write a valid claim, and never see one another. `require-up-to-date` has been off since 2026-08-10, so nothing even forces them to collide textually. **An earlier draft of this body argued the shared file is a mutex; that was wrong and the paragraph is deleted rather than softened.**

What R13 buys is narrower but real:

- an armed merge carries an **attributable, timestamped** claim, where the route previously recorded **nothing at all**;
- arming with **no** claim, or riding **another branch's**, **fails CI** — enforced, not exhorted, which is the failure mode BL-20260810 explicitly warns against (*"do NOT re-file an exhortation"*), and how its two predecessor lapse rows both closed "resolved" while the behaviour recurred anyway;
- it costs **no extra CI cycle** — the one half of BL-20260810 that no longer applies. That row assumed the mirror is a *separate* commit at merge time costing a ~9-minute restart; riding the arming push, the write is free.

**The real-time half is still missing and R13 cannot supply it.** The remedy is BL-20260810's own **option (a)** — a slot store not gated on merging — which is *the same artifact* **MI-182** needs for the successor board. Those are one piece of work, not two, and **PR #11334 (`claude/mi-182-board-cap-successor`) is already building it.** Concurrent-merge safety meanwhile rests where it already rested: branch-protection required status checks.

## ⚠️ Transition cost — two open PRs go red

`guards.yml` runs on `pull_request` with a plain `actions/checkout@v4`, which checks out the **merge ref**. So once R13 is on `main` it applies to open PRs immediately, without them changing:

| PR | branch | state |
|---|---|---|
| **#11348** | `claude/mgr-land-11279-0700-20260908` | `landing: self`, **armed**, no slot claim → **will fail R13** |
| **#11347** | `mi-168-post-merge-record` | `landing: self`, **armed**, no slot claim → **will fail R13** |

One commit each fixes it. **R13 is deliberately not grandfathered**, for R10's stated reason: arming is an affirmative act done today, and age excuses not knowing a rule but not asking to merge without a claim. The other two open PRs (#11337, #11334) declare `hold` and are unaffected. *(Population: all 5 open PRs at 2026-09-08T07:1xZ, this one included.)*

`session-board.json` is deliberately **not** added to `LANDING_MACHINERY`: every self-landing branch must now touch it, so listing it would make R12 fire on all of them and nothing could ever self-land again.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — no schema, model boundary, pipeline stage, API, inter-process contract or config shape is touched. CI-guard and docs only; no runtime, no order path.

## Test plan

- [x] `check_pr_landing.py --self-test` → **5 positive controls, 14 planted defects** (was 12). Fails closed both directions: armed holding *no* slot, and armed riding *another branch's* claim.
- [x] **Each pre-existing plant verified to still fire on its own rule, not incidentally on R13** — R4→`['R4']`, R5→`['R5']`, R12→`['R12']`, both new ones→`['R13']`, positive control→passes clean. A plant that passes for the wrong reason tests nothing.
- [x] `run_guards.py --base main` → **PASS 67 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 23**.
- [x] Four guards failed on the first run (`trainer-capture-watch`, `artifact-validity`, `operator-owed`, `layer-guard`) **only because `pytest` and `lint-imports` were absent from this container** — verified by installing both and re-running to 0 failures, not assumed.
- [x] No `--no-verify`, no force-push. Diff carries only its own landing file.
- [ ] CI green

## ⚠️ What this PR does NOT do

**It cannot demonstrate its own done-condition, by construction.** The work order asks that a PR satisfy R6 and the slot guard simultaneously *on a real PR*. This PR touches `check_pr_landing.py`, which is `LANDING_MACHINERY`, so **R12 forbids it from self-landing** — it is `landing: "hold"`, `hold_reason: "changes_landing_machinery"`, and a hold PR never reaches R6 at all. The end-to-end demonstration needs a *follow-on* Tier-1 docs-only PR that arms and claims together, after this lands. Claiming otherwise would be the presence-only marker this guard family exists to refuse.

## Governance — flagged, not resolved

The dispatch states this session owns the work order. **The object on `main` says otherwise**: `lifecycle: dormant`, `owner: null`, `blocked_on_basis: NOT_ASSESSED` — parked by its own terms ("a captured idea is PARKED, not queued — it becomes work only when it is given an owner and moved out of `dormant`"). Its `why` does record an operator spawn-priority exception dated 2026-09-08, but nobody moved it.

**I have deliberately left the object untouched.** Moving it out of `dormant` requires an owner and a TRUE `blocked_on` edge, and inventing either would be exactly the false-edge failure the schema warns about. The operator should set ownership if this is meant to be live.

No `▶️ START` was posted to #6927: it is at the 2500-comment cap and writes 403 (MI-182, known/parked, not retried).

## Verdict on the work order

Both invariants hold **partially**: R6 untouched; the slot invariant restored as an **audited, fail-closed** claim but **not as real-time exclusion**. Per the work order's own terms — *"if the two invariants are genuinely irreconcilable as stated, bring it as a decision with the trade-off named"* — that residue is the decision, and the trade-off is named above.

## Filed for follow-ups

- The end-to-end demonstration PR described above.
- **MI-182 is the blocker of record here**, not an unrelated parked row — its successor board is what restores the live claim alongside R13's durable one.
